rationale: Oko's ability sets the object's creature type, and 205.1a says a set subtype replaces existing subtypes (so the Food type is gone); 109.2 supplies the other half, that Gilded Goose's 'sacrifice a Food' means a permanent with that subtype. Both facts are needed, so 'all'.

Answer has two independent halves: leaves-the-battlefield triggers look back in time (603.10 states the principle, 603.10a puts LTB abilities on the list - either states it), and the intervening 'if' is rechecked on resolution (603.4 or its resolution-side restatement 608.2a). Both halves are required, alternatives inside each.

Ordering of the two cast-triggers on the stack comes from APNAP trigger placement (603.3b, or the general APNAP rule 101.4), and the copies dodging Chalice comes from 707.10 stating a copy of a spell isn't cast. Both required.

The ability on the stack is its own object, separate from its source and legally targetable (113.7a / 109.1 / 115.2 each state a piece of that), and hexproof only stops the permanent itself from being targeted (702.11b). Need one of the first group plus the hexproof rule.

Whole answer is target legality rechecked on resolution: once Autumn controls the Soldiers, Tempted by the Oriq's only targets are illegal and it's removed from the stack, which is exactly what 608.2b states.

The answer rests on each resolution of Aminatou's Augury creating its own separate effect, so its 'a spell of each type' permission is tracked per effect; 609.1 is the only chunk that states a resolving spell creates effects of its own. Low confidence - the CR has no rule squarely on point.

The discard still happens; only the destination is replaced, and 400.7j states that when an effect moves an object to a public zone (exile), other parts of that effect can still find it, which is why Seasoned Pyromancer counts the discarded cards.

701.21a states a player can't sacrifice a permanent they don't control, and 118.12a states that '[do something] unless [a player does something else]' means the default action happens when the optional action isn't taken. Both are needed to get to '2 damage'.
113.7a states an activated or triggered ability exists on the stack independently of its source and that removing the source doesn't affect it - that is the entire answer.

613.5 states continuous-effect changes are applied continually and instantaneously (so the +2/+2 from its own ability is already there), and 704.3 states SBAs are only checked when a player would get priority, so there is never a moment with lethal toughness.

Three separate facts: the attack cost is determined and paid inside the declare attackers turn-based action (any of 508.1h/i/j), Deathrite Shaman's targeted ability isn't a mana ability so it can't be activated there (605.1a), and mana from the beginning of combat step is gone by then (106.4).

'Enters with' is a replacement effect (614.1c) and 614.12 states the game works out how the permanent enters before it enters, which is why Rhizome Lurcher is still a creature card in the graveyard and counts itself.

Shade's Form's trigger is a leaves-the-battlefield/dies trigger, and the look-back-in-time exception is what makes it trigger off a mass destruction that also killed the Aura; 603.10 states the principle and 603.10a lists LTB abilities, so either one is a correct hit.

The judge walks the layer system: layer order (613.1 and the layer 6/7 entries), the rule that an effect already applying keeps applying after its ability is removed (613.6), layer 7 sublayer order setting-before-modifying (613.4/b/c), timestamp order inside layer 6 (613.7), and the absence of a dependency (613.8a). Each is a distinct required step with interchangeable statements inside.

The Phyrexian life-or-mana choice is announced while casting (601.2b, with 107.4f stating the symbol can be paid either way), and Trinisphere's increase is applied afterward when the total cost is determined and locked in (601.2f).

The chain works because a copy acquires the original's copiable values including its copy ability (707.2) and 'enters as a copy' choices happen as it enters (707.5); the answer is that the Sakashima-style ability can only choose a creature, so copying the Animate Dead enchantment is not a legal choice. Low confidence: no CR chunk states the creature-only restriction directly.
The judge cites it outright: 702.140a states a spell cast for its mutate cost becomes a mutating creature spell, so it's still a creature spell and Withering Boon can counter it.

712.18 states a double-faced permanent that transforms doesn't become a new object and effects applying to it keep applying - that is exactly why Karn's Touch's animation survives the transform into Sanctum of the Sun.

Three facts, all needed: the returning Aura's controller chooses a legal object as it enters (303.4f), protection from black stops it enchanting Cemetery Gate (702.16c), and hexproof only prevents targeting, which attaching isn't (702.11b).

Dredge is a replacement effect for the draw (702.52a), and 616.1/616.1e state the affected player picks which competing replacement effect to apply, after which the draw event no longer exists for the other one.

Splice only adds the spliced card's rules text to the spell (702.47a), and Evermind's blue comes from a color indicator, which is a separate characteristic rather than rules text (204.2). Both are needed for 'the spell doesn't become blue'.
Gisa and Geralf returns as a new object with no memory of its previous existence (400.7), so its once-per-turn cast permission is a fresh effect.
903.9a states a commander that was put into exile may be moved to the command zone by its owner as a state-based action, which is the whole answer regardless of the card being face down.

Split second lets mana abilities through (702.61a states the restriction excludes mana abilities, 702.61b says so explicitly), Lion's Eye Diamond's ability qualifies as a mana ability (605.1a), and 'activate only as an instant' just means having priority (304.5).
608.2c states the controller follows the spell's instructions in the order written, so Winding Constrictor is exiled before the counters are placed and can't boost them.

The controller chooses the order of the competing enters-with-counters replacement effects (616.1/616.1e/616.1f), but 614.5 states a replacement effect only gets one opportunity, so Hardened Scales can only add one counter. Both halves required.

X is announced while casting (601.2b) and Sphere of Resistance's increase is added when the total cost is determined and locked in (601.2f), giving the two-mana payment that lets two colors be spent. Targeting is unrestricted, so no separate target rule is required.

609.4b states 'spend mana as though it were mana of any color' only changes how a cost may be paid and isn't an alternative cost, and 702.137a states spectacle is an alternative cost. Both needed to conclude the two don't conflict.

Casting as an Adventure evaluates only the alternative characteristics (715.3a), which is the same rule stated generally in 601.3e; either chunk supports that Haakon's Knight-only permission doesn't cover the Adventure half.

Two competing copy-as-it-enters replacement effects: the affected player picks the order and then repeats the process (616.1/616.1c/616.1f), and whichever copy effect is applied last sets the copiable values (707.2/707.3), so neither order gives Quakestrider Ceratops.
The 1/3 split is announced as the spell is cast (601.2d), and Obosh's 'instead' doubling is a replacement effect (614.1a) that applies to the three damage headed for Nevaeh, making it six.
The grant and the removal of infect are both layer 6 effects applied in timestamp order (613.7/613.7b), and the judge's parenthetical is the dependency test failing (613.8a). Both required.
712.16 states double-faced permanents can't be turned face down and that such an effect does nothing - the entire answer.

Four separate mana-value facts the answer needs: copies copy mana cost (707.2), a token has only the characteristics its creating effect defines so it has no mana cost (111.3), an object with no mana cost has mana value 0 (202.3a), and a transformed nonmodal double-faced permanent uses its front face while a copy of a back face is 0 (202.3b).

614.12 states you check the permanent's characteristics as it would exist on the battlefield when applying enters-the-battlefield replacement effects, without treating it as already there - so Minas Tirith would be a creature but isn't yet a legendary creature you control.

Both effects are type-changing (613.1d), so they apply in timestamp order (613.7/613.7a) with Magus of the Moon last, and 305.7 states setting a land's basic type strips its old types and abilities and grants the new mana ability, giving only {R}.

The trigger's 'that artifact' is the object identified by its trigger condition when it triggered, and 608.2k states such an untargeted reference still points at that object afterwards; moving the Aura later doesn't redirect it.

614.12 states the game checks the permanent's characteristics as it would exist on the battlefield, including its own static abilities, so Erebos would be a noncreature and Blind Obedience's replacement never applies.

Memory Lapse's 'put it on top of its owner's library instead' is a self-replacement effect, and both 614.15 and 616.1a state self-replacement effects are applied before other replacement effects; either chunk answers it.

Regeneration is a shield that replaces the next destruction and taps the creature and removes damage (701.19a), destruction from lethal damage only happens when SBAs are checked, which is when a player would get priority (704.3), and Prismari Command's modes happen in written order (608.2c). All three required.

106.6a states that when a replacement effect increases the mana produced, a separate delayed triggered ability is created for each mana produced - exactly the Mana Reflection plus Pyromancer's Goggles case.

707.9e states that when a copy effect with an exception (Spark Double's extra +1/+1 counter) is followed by another copy effect applied to the object, the exception's effect doesn't happen - so only the final application's counter survives.

702.69a states gravestorm copies the spell for each permanent put into a graveyard from the battlefield this turn, and 608.2h states the effect gets its information when it's applied (on resolution), so the sacrifice made in response is counted.

The attack question is the summoning sickness rule, which asks whether the creature has been controlled continuously since the turn began (302.6); 727.1 supplies that Karn's ability restarts the game and a new game begins with that player's turn, so the creature is there before the turn starts.

106.7 states 'could produce' includes any mana an ability of that permanent would produce if it resolved, ignoring whether the ability's costs could be paid - which is the whole answer for Throne of Makindi with no charge counters.

Drought counts {B} symbols in the spell's mana cost, which is what's printed on the card (202.1/202.1a); 601.2f states cost increases like Derelor's are part of the total cost, not the mana cost. Any of these states that what was paid doesn't change the mana cost.

Both effects are type-changing and so share layer 4 (613.1d), which is a precondition of dependency; 613.8a defines the dependency test the judge runs and 613.8b states the dependent effect waits, so Blood Moon applies first and Life and Limb never applies.

122.2 states counters cease to exist on a zone change (Skullbriar's own ability is the exception while it has it), and manifesting makes it a face-down 2/2 with no text (701.40a, restated by 708.2/708.2a), so the ability is gone and the counters vanish as it enters.
111.2 states the player who creates a token is its owner, even though Gather Specimens made it enter under Nico's control, so Homeward Path gives it to Asa.

Squandered Resources asks what mana the land could produce, defined by 106.7, and Blood Moon setting the land's subtype to Mountain strips its old abilities and grants only the {R} mana ability (305.7). Both needed to get 'just {R}'.
